newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close higher after see-saw session.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close higher after see-saw session.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended stronger on Thursday after see-sawing in a wide range, caught between optimism after Wednesday's surge in prices but caution ahead of the release of fresh U.S. economic data, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index rose 72.09 points to 12,477.56 after slipping into negative territory early in the session to a low of 12,377.88 and rising to a high of 12,496.57.

"On the one hand local shares just followed yesterday's rebound and continue to fare quite well but on the other hand I think investors are still concerned about the U.S. figures," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
The Hang Seng index rose 213.30 points on Wednesday.
Market turnover was HK$6.34 billion on Thursday, down from Wednesday's HK$7.48 billion.
September U.S. personal income and consumption data are due on Thursday and the October U.S. jobs report on Friday.

"I think the market has made its move for this week and I think it is going to sit around and wait for some of the data coming out," said Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

Property stocks were the strongest performers on Thursday. Cheung Kong rose HK$1.00 to HK$62.00, Sun Hung Kai Properties gained HK$0.75 to HK$88.00 and New World Development advanced HK$0.70 to HK$45.00.

"I think property stocks were sought after because before the end of the year there may be major property companies like Cheung Kong offering a bunch of units in major projects. People are expecting quite a strong response to the sales," said Henri Lui, research analyst at Mansion House Securities.
Mobile telephone operator SmarTone Telecommunications Holdings Ltd made its stock market debut on Thursday and finished the session below its initial public offering price.

The stock opened at HK$17.25, level with its issue price, but closed at HK$16.50. Brokers said investors were concerned the stock had limited upside due to the low subscription level of the offering. The Hong Kong flotation was 2.95 times subscribed.

Shares in Whimsy Entertainment rose HK$0.18 to HK$1.97. The company said it had agreed to issue 28 million new shares at HK$1.50 a share to a substantial shareholder, raising net proceeds of about HK$41 million for general working capital.
